extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and organizations preparing FY25 MURI white papers and full proposals for DoD (ONR/AFOSR/ARO)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for submitting white papers and full proposals to the FY25 DoD MURI program, including registration/submission procedures, eligibility/administrative requirements, review criteria, and award administration. Targets academic and other research organizations seeking basic research funding from DoD components (ONR, AFOSR, ARO).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission requirement (Grants.gov)
rubrics_metrics.description: All Applicants shall submit their applications online through Grants.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DoD participates in Grants.gov initiative; white papers must NOT be submitted through Grants.gov (see separate FedConnect requirement).

rubrics_metrics.name: White paper submission channel
rubrics_metrics.description: White Papers must NOT be submitted through the Grants.gov application process. White paper submissions to ONR must be submitted through FedConnect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specific agency instruction (ONR uses FedConnect for white papers). Failure to use the correct channel may disqualify the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational registration requirements (SAM and Grants.gov account)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations must have an active System for Award Management (SAM) registration and Grants.gov account to apply for grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SAM registrations may take 7-10 days; register early. SAM registration must be renewed annually. Detailed registration instructions available on Grants.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants.gov profile and EBiz POC authorization / AOR role
rubrics_metrics.description: Add an organization profile to Grants.gov, have EBiz POC authorize profile roles, and ensure an Authorized Organization Representative (AOR) is assigned who can submit and make legally binding commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EBiz POC must authorize the AOR role; applicants cannot submit until AOR role is assigned. The AOR name is inserted as electronic signature on submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic signature rule
rubrics_metrics.description: When applications are submitted through Grants.gov, the name of the organization's AOR that submitted the application is inserted into the signature line of the application, serving as the electronic signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EBiz POC must authorize only individuals able to make legally binding commitments; missing this step can invalidate timely submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment file format requirement (PDF)
rubrics_metrics.description: All attachments to grant applications submitted through Grants.gov must be in Adobe Portable Document Format (PDF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals with attachments in other formats (word processing, spreadsheet, etc.) will not be considered for award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workspace usage and mandatory fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may use Grants.gov Workspace to create, edit, and submit applications; fields marked with an asterisk are mandatory and must be completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete SF-424 fields first to populate common fields across forms. Workspace allows multiple participants and shows progress; applicants can download individual PDF forms if desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission timing recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants.gov recommends submitting at least 24-48 hours prior to the close date; DoD strongly recommends submitting no later than two (2) business days ahead of deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows time to correct potential technical issues. Applicants using unreliable internet connections should allow extra time for Workspace transfers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely receipt requirement and proof of submission
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications must be received by 5:00 PM Eastern Time on 6 September 2024; proof of timely submission is the Grants.gov electronic date/time stamp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants receive email acknowledgements and a Grants.gov Tracking Number. Applications received after the due date will be considered late and not considered for funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal receipt email sequence and statuses
rubrics_metrics.description: After submission the AOR will receive three emails: (1) submission confirmation page/time stamp, (2) Grants.gov validation receipt (or rejection) within two days, and (3) DoD acknowledgment of receipt (within ten days if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Tracking Number from email #1 to track submission. If validation fails, resubmit the application. Watch and save all three emails.

rubrics_metrics.name: White paper evaluation focus
rubrics_metrics.description: White papers will be evaluated to assess whether the proposed research is likely to meet the objectives of the specific topic and whether to encourage a full proposal submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment primarily focuses on scientific and technical merits, potential to significantly advance fundamental understanding, and potential DoD interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific and technical merits (evaluation criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific and technical merits of the proposed basic science and/or engineering research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators assess the technical rigor, clarity of objectives, and soundness of the scientific approach for basic research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential to significantly advance fundamental understanding (evaluation criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential for the research, if successful, to significantly advance fundamental understanding in the topic area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the MURI program is funded by a basic research appropriation, proposals must emphasize fundamental knowledge advancement rather than applied development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential DoD relevance and contribution to the DoD mission (evaluation criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential DoD relevance and contribution to the DoD mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should describe how the basic research could inform or support DoD needs and interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications and availability of the Principal Investigator and other investigators (evaluation criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualifications and availability of the Principal Investigator and other investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators consider investigators' expertise, prior accomplishments, and the time they will devote to the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of facilities and equipment (evaluation criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequacy of current or planned facilities and equipment to accomplish the research objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether institutional resources are sufficient or access to needed facilities is documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of interactions with other organizations (evaluation criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Impact of interactions with other organizations engaged in related research and development, particularly DoD laboratories, industry, and other organizations that perform research and development for defense applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider collaborations, partnerships, and potential synergies that could enhance the research impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realism and reasonableness of cost (evaluation criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Realism and reasonableness of cost (cost sharing is not a factor in the evaluation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget must be realistic for the proposed work; cost sharing will not influence evaluation scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation authority and process (review and selection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ultimate recommendation for award is made by the DoD scientific/technical community; recommended proposals are forwarded to Contracts and Grant Awards Management for cost analysis and responsibility determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recommendation does not guarantee an award; award depends on cost analysis, availability of funds, and other pre-award steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government will evaluate options for award purposes by adding total cost for all options to the total cost for the basic requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation of options does not obligate the Government to exercise options during performance; the Government reserves the right to exercise options at time of award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation panel composition and advisors
rubrics_metrics.description: White papers may be reviewed by the Research Topic Chief or by an evaluation panel chaired by the Research Topic Chief; panels consist of Government technical experts and may use external support contractors or advisors as subject-matter consultants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External contractors/advisors sign conflict of interest and non-disclosure agreements. Proposal selection and award decisions remain the responsibility of Government personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-stage evaluation (technical then cost)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals undergo a multi-stage evaluation: Government scientific experts evaluate technical proposals first; Government business professionals evaluate cost proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings are forwarded to senior DoD officials who make funding recommendations; cost evaluation and applicant responsibility checks follow technical selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possibility of partial selection and adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation panels may recommend funding less than an entire MURI proposal (partial awards) due to factors like insufficient funds, research overlap, or synergies; adjustments will be agreed with the PI prior to final award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Government may select subsets of multi-investigator proposals; negotiation will occur before final award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient qualifications (32 CFR 22.415 standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be qualified, a potential recipient must: (i) have management capability and adequate financial and technical resources; (ii) have a satisfactory record of executing such programs (if a prior recipient); (iii) have a satisfactory record of integrity and business ethics; and (iv) be otherwise qualified and eligible to receive a grant under applicable laws and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants Officer determines recipient qualification prior to award; applicants should provide information to assist this determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAPIIS and integrity/performance information review
rubrics_metrics.description: For awards with total Federal share greater than the simplified acquisition threshold, the Federal awarding agency will review and consider information in FAPIIS (via SAM) prior to making an award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may review and comment on FAPIIS entries about themselves; agencies consider applicant comments when assessing applicant risk per 2 CFR 200.205.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal award notice and award instrument
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants will receive notification emails advising if their proposal was selected; notification is not authorization to commit funds. The award document signed by the Contracting or Grants Officer is the official authorizing instrument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award/modification documents distribution differs by agency: ARO/AFOSR email awards; ONR awards available via EDA/Piee system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Export control compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must ensure compliance with all U.S. export control laws and regulations, including ITAR (22 CFR Parts 120-130) and EAR (15 CFR Parts 730-774), and address in proposals whether ITAR or EAR restrictions apply to the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are responsible for obtaining any required licenses or approvals (including deemed exports) and should consult regulations and guidance (ecfr, export.gov).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of animals (requirements before award)
rubrics_metrics.description: If animals will be used, the Applicant must submit a Full Appendix or Abbreviated Appendix with supporting documentation (e.g., IACUC Approval, IACUC Approved Protocol, most recent USDA Inspection Report) prior to award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DoD policy references DoDI 3216.01 and implementing instruction DHA-MSR 6025.02; contact agency Animal Use Administrators for assistance. Documentation required prior to award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects protections and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must protect rights and welfare of human subjects and comply with the Common Rule at 32 CFR part 219 and DoD Instruction 3216.02; prior to award, submit IRB approval, informed consent documents, proof of human research training, and DHHS-issued Federal Wide Assurance (FWA) or documentation of exemption/determination where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit documentation to the DoD Agency HRPO via the Program Officer; HRPO has final judgment. Research involving human subjects must not begin until HRPO approval is received; Government will not reimburse work performed in violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosafety and biosecurity compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must comply with DODM 6055.18 and at least the minimum applicable requirements of CDC BMBL and NIH Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure institutional biosafety and biosecurity standards meet current editions of referenced documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recombinant/synthetic nucleic acid research documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must not begin performance of research within the scope of the NIH Guidelines until ONR has reviewed and accepted applicant documentation, including a written statement of compliance, evidence of IBC approval (or exemption), and DHHS letter of approval or compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The compliance statement should be on institutional letterhead and made by an institutional official other than the PI. Provide documentation as part of the proposal prior to award where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Dual Use Research of Concern (DURC) compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions and USG funding agencies subject to the USG Policy for Institutional Oversight of Life Sciences Dual Use Research of Concern must comply with all listed requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposals involve certain biological agents or toxins, contact the Technical Point of Contact and consult S3 guidance (http://www.phe.gov/s3/dualuse).

rubrics_metrics.name: DoD High Performance Computing Program (HPCMP) access
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees of ONR grants and other assistance instruments may be eligible to use HPCMP assets if ONR Program Officer approval is obtained and security/screening requirements are completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional information and application available at https://www.hpc.mil/.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project and program review meetings budgeting and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should budget for two in-person Project Review Meetings per year; Program Review Meetings may be held once per year and last two to three days. Meetings may be in-person or virtual as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may offer to host Program Review Meetings (include specific offer language and estimated cost). Inclusion of hosting language is optional and will not affect selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act (FFATA) reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Entities applying for financial assistance must provide information describing processes and systems to comply with subaward and executive total compensation reporting requirements codified in 2 CFR Part 170 (Appendix A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report unless an exception/exemption applies. Refer to 2 CFR Part 170 and Appendix A for details on requirements and exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Assistance Certifications and disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must submit required certifications (e.g., SF-LLL Disclosure of Lobbying) and disclose unpaid delinquent tax liability or felony convictions where applicable via SF-424 (R&R) block 17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checking 'I Agree' on SF-424 block 17 attests compliance with specified statutes; false or missing certifications can affect eligibility. AFOSR-specific note: checking 'I Agree' certifies no lobbying activity to disclose for grants > $100,000 unless SF-LLL attached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications regarding restrictions on lobbying (>$100,000)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant awards greater than $100,000 require a certification of compliance with national policy concerning lobbying via electronic submission of SF-424 (R&R) block 17; if lobbying activity exists, attach SF-LLL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete SF-LLL if required and follow instructions for that form. Failure to provide required lobbying disclosures may affect award eligibility.
